statusLabel: Returning Archetype — GX-era, reworked in CORI
summary: Uria, Hamon, and Raviel — the GX-era Sacred Beasts — return with new incarnations that can ONLY be Special Summoned via a "Sacred Beast" card effect, dropping their old, brutally restrictive original summoning conditions. New support makes the trio far more consistent to assemble. Note: Yugipedia treats the new CORI "Sacred Beast" (singular) cards as a distinct card family from the original GX-era "Sacred Beasts" (plural) — thematically linked and fully playable together, but technically two different archetype tags.

cards.name: Uria, Lord of Searing Flames
cards.effectText: Full print name: "Inferno of the Sacred Beasts – Uria, Lord of Searing Flames" (CORI-EN005). Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set; must be Special Summoned by a "Sacred Beast" card's effect. Reveal this card in your hand: add 1 "Sacred Beast" Trap from your Deck to your hand, then discard 1 card. Gains 1000 ATK/DEF for each Trap in either GY. Once per turn (Quick Effect): target 1 Spell/Trap on the field and destroy it; neither player can respond. Attribute/race/ATK/DEF are pattern-matched from Hamon/Raviel and the archetype's own tutor text, not independently re-verified against a primary source.

cards.name: Hamon, Lord of Striking Thunder
cards.effectText: Full print name: "Calamity of the Sacred Beasts – Hamon, Lord of Striking Thunder" (CORI-EN006). Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set; must be Special Summoned by a "Sacred Beast" card's effect. Reveal this card in your hand: add 1 "Sacred Beast" Spell from your Deck to your hand, then discard 1 card. Once per turn, if a monster is sent to your opponent's GY: inflict 1000 damage to your opponent. If this card is destroyed by battle or by an effect: you take no damage this turn.

cards.name: Raviel, Lord of Phantasms
cards.effectText: Full print name: "Infinity of the Sacred Beasts – Raviel, Lord of Phantasms" (CORI-EN007). Cannot be Normal Summoned/Set; must be Special Summoned by a "Sacred Beast" card's effect. Reveal this card in your hand: add 1 "Sacred Beast" monster (except itself) from your Deck to your hand, then discard 1 card. Once per turn (Quick Effect): Tribute 2 other "Sacred Beast" monsters; destroy as many monsters your opponent controls as possible, and if you do, this card gains 1000 ATK for each monster destroyed.

cards.name: The Orchestrator of the Sacred Beasts
cards.effectText: The archetype's key enabler. Each effect once per turn. (1) Reveal this card in your hand; discard 1 card, and if you do, Special Summon 1 "Sacred Beast" monster from your hand in Defense Position, except a Level 8 monster. (2) Discard 1 card; Special Summon 1 "Sacred Beast" monster from your hand or GY in Defense Position, except a Level 8 monster or the card you just discarded. (3) Banish this card from your GY; Special Summon 1 "Sacred Beast" monster from your GY in Defense Position, except a Level 8 monster.

cards.name: Martyr of the Sacred Beasts
cards.effectText: Each effect once per turn. If this card is Normal or Special Summoned: place 1 "Sacred Beast" Field Spell or Continuous Spell/Trap from your Deck face-up on the field. If you control another "Sacred Beast" monster: Special Summon 2 copies of this card from your hand, Deck, and/or GY. During your opponent's End Phase, if you have this card and a Level 10 "Sacred Beast" monster in your GY: add this card to your hand.

cards.name: Fallen Paradise of the Sacred Beasts
cards.effectText: Up to 3 times per turn, during your Main Phase: send 3 other cards of the same card type (Monster, Spell, or Trap) from your hand and/or face-up field to the GY, then Special Summon 1 "Sacred Beast" monster from your hand, Deck, GY, or banishment, unaffected by your opponent's activated Spell/Trap effects. Once per turn, if you control a "Sacred Beast" monster with original Level 10: draw 2 cards.

cards.name: Unleashing the Sacred Beasts
cards.effectText: Each effect once per turn. (1) Add 3 differently-named "Sacred Beast" monsters from your Deck to your hand, then discard 2 cards. (2) Banish this card from your GY, except the turn it was sent there: add 1 Level 10 Pyro, Thunder, or Fiend monster that cannot be Normal Summoned/Set from your Deck to your hand.

cards.name: Phantasmal Sacred Beasts of Chaos
cards.effectText: The trio's new boss Fusion. Materials: 3 Level 10 monsters that cannot be Normal Summoned/Set (i.e. Uria, Hamon, and Raviel). Fusion Summon, or Special Summon from your Extra Deck by sending those materials you control to the GY; once per turn either way. The first 2 times this card would be destroyed by a card effect each turn, it is not destroyed. Once per Chain, up to 3 times per turn (Quick Effect): target 1 face-up monster your opponent controls; negate its effects until the end of this turn, then gain LP equal to half its ATK.

comboLines.title: Orchestrator into a Level 10 boss
comboLines.body: Unleashing the Sacred Beasts loads your hand with all three bosses, then The Orchestrator of the Sacred Beasts or Fallen Paradise of the Sacred Beasts breaks the "cannot Special Summon except by a Sacred Beast effect" restriction to actually put one on the field. Once a Level 10 Sacred Beast is out, Fallen Paradise's card-draw clause keeps refueling your hand, and if you can assemble all three bosses on board (or send them from field to GY as Fallen Paradise fodder), Phantasmal Sacred Beasts of Chaos turns them into a single 5000 ATK/DEF Fusion with repeatable effect negation.

sampleDecklist.label: Core archetype package (all quantities below the staple line) sourced from a community list dated this week, "Sacred Beast (July 2026)" by Mr_Reinoheart (cardcluster.com/deck/3XeobL) — the most concrete, dated sample list found for this archetype; still not an official tournament Top Cut list. A generic staple package was added to round out to a legal 40, and 2x Phantasmal Sacred Beasts of Chaos was added to the Extra Deck since the sourced list predates that card's confirmation. ⚠ Banlist watch: this list runs 1x Called by the Grave, which was made Forbidden in the OCG's July 1, 2026 update; the TCG's most recent banlist predates Chaos Origins, so it should still be legal for NAWCQ, but double-check before finalizing your deck list.
